content: The Bleed Purple Foundation is a recognized charitable organization under section 501(c)(3) of the IRS code, based in Denver, Colorado. It was established in 2005 by members of the Theta Zeta chapter of the Delta Tau Delta International Fraternity. The foundation was created to support one of their fraternity brothers who had been diagnosed with stage III-B Hodgkin's Lymphoma. As a demonstration of fraternity brotherhood and unwavering solidarity, the members organized a head-shaving auction on the University of San Diego campus. This event successfully raised over $4,000 to assist their brother in need. This marked the inception of the Bleed Purple Foundation. The mission of Bleed Purple is to provide support to college students who are battling cancer. For many college students, managing financial responsibilities is already a significant challenge. Between attending classes, participating in campus organizations, completing unpaid internships, and engaging in late-night study sessions, finding time for a job that covers basic living expenses—let alone medical bills—can be nearly impossible. Bleed Purple aims to unite the Greek community in a collective effort to support college students diagnosed with cancer. The primary objective of the foundation is to alleviate the financial burdens faced by these students, which are often exacerbated by the costs associated with their illness.
